items.text: People often say that the stars govern their fate but they forget the fact that success  or  failure  is  the  result  of  one's  own (238)________. If we sow chaff, we can't reap grain; and the result or consequence of an action depends on what one does and to the extent he (239)________ it. If we work hard, we succeed only to  the  extent  that  we  work.  People  who  think  that  the  law  of karma  is  (240)________  may  feel  that  if  one  is  destined  to  get something  he  will  always get it whether he strives for it or not. But  experience  tells  us  that  reward  and  punishments  are  the direct  result  of  our  action.  Honesty  and  hard  work  never  go unrewarded and (241)________ and evil deeds never go (242)________. In fact even the law of karma, in its proper sense, means that  the  fruit  we  get is decided by whatever actions we did in the past.

Gandhi,  (243)_________  father  of  the  Indian  nation,  practiced 'ahimsa' in his personal and political life. He firmly believed that non-violence is not meant merely for monks, saints and priests; it is for commoners too. If violence is the law of the (244)_______-beasts, non-violence  is  the  law  of  the  civilised human  species.  'The  spirit  of  the  brute  is  inactive  and  so  he knows no law; he knows only physical might. The dignity of man requires  obedience  to  a  higher  law,  to  strength  of  the  spirit,' Gandhi said. Ahimsa, to Gandhiji, meant that one should love all;

even (245)________ enemies. And the expression of love, ahimsa, should  be  in  such  a  manner  that  it  impresses  itself  indelibly upon the so-called enemy, and then the enemy must return that love.  It  is  a  practically  (246)________  philosophy.  Gandhi  was realistic; he believed  that  non-violence  provides  the  fullest protection  to  one's  self-respect  and  sense  of  humour.  It  won't work in the defence of (247)_______ gains and immoral acts. He called  his marches off when people indulged in violence during protests  for  India's  freedom.  His  faith  in  'ahimsa'  played  an influential role in enabling the creation of an independent India in 1947,  with  minimum  bloodshed,  breaking  the  shackles  framed by the British.

Earthquake  is  the  (248)_________ breaking and displacement of substantial  portions  of  the  earth's  outer  rocky crust. During an earthquake,  rock  disturbances can cause rivers to change their flow.  Landslides  (249)__________  by  earthquakes  can  cause significant destruction and loss of life. Tsunamis are a (250)_________ of damaging waves caused by large earthquakes that  occur  under  the  ocean.  Earthquakes  rarely  directly  kill anyone. Many (251)__________ and injuries are caused by falling debris  and  the  fall  of  structures.  The  (252)_________  of  an earthquake  relies  on  how  much  and  how  far  rock  cracks  and shifts.

- Q.249. (a) triggered  (b) subdued  (c) blocked  (d) prevented
